source.title: Activity of serotonin-containing neurons in nucleus raphe magnus in freely moving cats

confidence_rationale: Classic in-vivo single-unit recording with pharmacological identification (Jacobs lab, independent of the Hobson lineage that dominates the existing MECH-204 entries). Quantitatively pins the depth of the REM serotonergic withdrawal: identified serotonergic neurons fire at 4.49 spikes/s in active waking, 2.14 in SWS, and 0.20 in REM -- an ~95% reduction that grounds the 'zero-point' premise. Held below 0.8 because the recorded nucleus is raphe magnus (a bulbospinal / pain-modulatory nucleus), not the forebrain-projecting dorsal raphe that carries the precision-relevant tone, and because the paper documents the SUBSTRATE FACT of withdrawal, not the active-vs-permissive functional role that is the live MECH-204 conflict.
failure_signatures: If precision-relevant 5-HT tone during REM is carried by dorsal-raphe or median-raphe subpopulations that do NOT go fully silent (the ~12% atypical DR neurons documented by Sakai & Crochet 2001), the near-zero raphe magnus rate would overstate the depth of the forebrain zero-point and the strict tonic_5ht=0 idealisation would need softening.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Serotonin-containing neurons in nucleus raphe magnus of freely moving cats, identified on-line by slow regular spontaneous activity and inhibition by a 5-HT agonist, discharged fastest during active waking (4.49 +/- 0.40 spikes/s), intermediate during slow-wave sleep (2.14 +/- 0.23), and slowest during REM sleep (0.20 +/- 0.03 spikes/s).
mapping.ree_translation: Independent quantitative substrate evidence for the premise MECH-204 builds on: at REM entry serotonergic raphe output collapses to near zero, which is the biological correlate of SerotoninModule._tonic_5ht -> 0 and the moment MECH-204 says the recalibration zero-point is defined. Fornal's ~95% withdrawal figure calibrates 'how close to zero' the REE idealisation should be treated as.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Nucleus raphe magnus is a caudal, largely bulbospinal/antinociceptive serotonergic nucleus, not the dorsal raphe that projects to the forebrain circuits carrying precision priors; the paper is cited here as corroboration that the REM-off serotonergic pattern is a pan-raphe rule, NOT as direct evidence about forebrain precision tone (that role is held by the existing Sakai & Crochet 2001 DR entry). Critically, this paper is silent on the active-vs-permissive question -- it establishes THAT 5-HT withdraws, not whether that withdrawal actively calibrates a reference or merely permits recalibration.
mapping.source_context: In-vivo extracellular single-unit recording in freely-moving cats across the sleep-wake cycle, with serotonergic identity confirmed by inhibitory response to the 5-HT agonist 5-MeO-DMT. Cat -> human -> REE transfer rests on the well-conserved mammalian raphe-REM-quiescence pattern.

confidence_components.notes: Methodologically strong classic ephys with pharmacological ID. Mapping fidelity moderate because raphe magnus is not the forebrain-relevant DR nucleus and the paper speaks to the substrate premise, not the consumer/functional conflict. Transfer risk moderate (cat->human) but the pattern is well-conserved.
